item.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway Networking Requirements for Private MCP and REST APIs
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway Networking Requirements for Private MCP and REST APIs

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway now supports agents that call internal REST APIs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, provided they meet specific network ownership and traffic inspection requirements.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. The Gateway connects to private targets through an Amazon VPC Lattice resource gateway. This update clarifies where to place the resource gateway, who owns each network component, and the configuration decisions required for traffic to cross a central firewall in both directions.

🧩 How it works

The AgentCore Gateway reaches private targets through two private endpoint modes:

  • Managed mode: AgentCore creates the resource gateway for you. This fits environments where the Gateway account can own the subnets it runs in.
  • Self-managed mode: You create the resource gateway and give the target a resource configuration. As documented, this places it in subnets with direct access to the backend, fitting environments that do not require inspection between the Gateway and the tool.

In the pattern built and tested in the US East (N. Virginia) AWS Region (us-east-1), the network account owns the resource gateway and places it in subnets routed through AWS Transit Gateway. This ensures every request and reply between VPCs crosses the central firewall in an inspection VPC. The network team keeps ownership of every subnet, and traffic between the Gateway and private APIs and MCP servers crosses the central firewall in both directions.

⚙️ Key details

The architecture relies on specific VPC Lattice objects and sharing mechanisms:

  • Resource gateway: The Amazon VPC Lattice entry point into a VPC, utilizing elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in subnets you choose.
  • Resource configuration: A VPC Lattice object that names one backend (an internal load balancer or VPC endpoint DNS name and port) behind a resource gateway. This can be shared with other accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).

Key ownership and traffic rules include:

  • A network account owns every VPC, subnet, and AWS Transit Gateway attachment, sharing application subnets through AWS RAM.
  • The Gateway account can own subnets that reach your tools.
  • The Gateway and application accounts build only in subnets shared to them through AWS RAM.
  • Tools are reachable on public endpoints if central inspection is not required for that specific flow, but in the documented pattern, every flow between VPCs crosses the central firewall.
  • The central firewall in the inspection VPC inspects the traffic between the Gateway and your private APIs and MCP servers.

🚀 Availability

The pattern was validated in a lab with three member accounts and a management account in AWS Organizations. The AWS CloudFormation templates, test scripts, test evidence, and reference material (address plan, full validation checks, troubleshooting, quotas) are available in the companion repository.

#AmazonBedrock #AgentCore #AI #Networking #MCP

Source: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users
item.description:
Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users

Verlihub is an advanced NMDC+S protocol server for Linux and Windows operating systems. It offers a high-performance solution with low RAM and CPU usage, capable of holding more than 25,000 users.

🔍 Overview

Verlihub provides high-level functionality for managing connections, hub administration, and security features. It uses epoll on Linux and Windows, and supports worker threads for slow work to maintain performance efficiency.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resource Efficiency: Low RAM and CPU usage using epoll on both Linux and Windows operating systems.
  • Capacity: Able to hold more than 25,000 users.
  • Security: Built-in TLS-encrypted connections using OpenSSL, supporting plain and encrypted users on the same port. An external TLS proxy is also supported, sending the real address of the user with the $MyIP command.
  • Database Support: Offers backup and restore functionality for MySQL or MariaDB databases.
  • Customization and Localization: Allows extending functionality via Lua scripts (including HTTP requests) and supports hub messages in many languages.
  • User and Connection Management: Handles user management with privileges, clients and connections management, and logging of user IPs and complete MyINFOs (requires Ledokol).
  • GeoIP Integration: Tracks the GeoIP country, city, and ASN of users using MaxMindDB.
  • Statistics: Generates statistics for your hub (requires Ledokol).

🚀 Availability

Verlihub builds on Windows with MinGW-w64, with dependencies and build steps detailed in Install.md. TLS support is built-in using OpenSSL and enabled by default; to build without it, the -DUSE_TLS=OFF flag can be used.

Several resources are available for support and integration:

  • Website: https://github.com/verlihub
  • Wiki: https://github.com/verlihub/verlihub/wiki
  • Crash: https://crash.verlihub.net
  • Translate: https://explore.transifex.com/feardc/verlihub
  • Ledokol: https://ledo.feardc.net
  • MMDB: https://ledo.feardc.net/mmdb
  • Support: nmdcs://hub.verlihub.net:7777
  • Hublist: https://te-home.net/?do=hublist

#Verlihub #NMDC #ServerSoftware #OpenSource #Networking

Source: Verlihub/verlihub

item.title: Marvell to Showcase AI Data Center Connectivity and Memory Solutions
item.description:
Marvell to Showcase AI Data Center Connectivity and Memory Solutions

Marvell Technology, Inc. has announced it will present its portfolio of AI data center connectivity and memory solutions at the AI Infra Summit 2026, taking place September 15 to 17 in Santa Clara, California.

⚙️ Key details

Marvell will highlight advances in its end-to-end data center connectivity portfolio for scale-up, scale-out, and scale-across applications at Booth #704. The showcase includes:

Solution Function/Capability
Marvell® Photonic Fabric™ Technology Enables memory sharing across multiple racks, extending scale beyond traditional distance constraints
Marvell RELIANT™ Interconnect Telemetry Platform Provides real-time visibility into the health and performance of AI data center infrastructure connectivity across optical and electrical links
Marvell Teralynx® T100 102 Tbps Ethernet switch device delivering increased bandwidth and efficiency for large-scale AI networks
PCIe 6.0 Switch 256-lane design to connect more accelerators and devices within scale-up AI systems
CXL-based memory solutions Supports expansion, compression, pooling, and near-memory acceleration to reduce dataset movement between XPUs and accelerate large-scale vector databases
DPUs and Ethernet switching Deliver high-performance access to NVMe storage across the network
PCIe® 6.0 NVMe SSD controller Optimized for next-generation enterprise and AI storage

🔍 Overview

During the summit, Marvell executives will participate in panels and presentations regarding connectivity and networking for next-generation AI data center infrastructure. This includes a keynote presentation titled “AI Inference at Scale” delivered by Dave Lazovsky, Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center Networking Business Group.

#Marvell #AIDataCenter #Semiconductors #Networking #AIInfraSummit

Source: Marvell to Showcase End-to-End AI Data Center Connectivity Portfolio at AI Infra Summit 2026
